gameOver.message: Player GLM47 Spike is the winner

annotations.description: Tiger-Seal is a 3/3 with vigilance but taps itself at the beginning of your upkeep, meaning it can't attack unless you draw a second card each turn to untap it. Fear of Missing Out is a 2/3 that provides card filtering (discard/draw) on ETB and has delirium synergy for extra combat phases. With only Island and Multiversal Passage as remaining land drops (no blue mana source beyond Spirebluff Canal already in play), casting Tiger-Seal uses the blue mana but results in a creature that will be tapped down most turns without reliable second-card-draw triggers. Fear of Missing Out would have been better as it provides immediate card selection (looting on ETB), can actually attack as a 2/3 without self-tapping restrictions, and contributes to delirium. The Tiger-Seal will likely just sit tapped doing nothing for several turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tiger-Seal, a 3/3 that taps itself each upkeep and needs second-card-draw triggers to untap.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fear of Missing Out to get card filtering (discard/draw ETB) and a creature that can reliably attack. This also starts building toward delirium for extra combat phases later.

annotations.description: Playing Multiversal Passage (which costs 2 life to enter untapped or enters tapped) instead of Hushwood Verge is suboptimal. Breeding Pool is a Forest, so Hushwood Verge would enter untapped and produce both G and W. Playing Hushwood Verge as the land drop preserves the option to play Multiversal Passage later (potentially for a different color) and avoids paying 2 life. Additionally, with Hushwood Verge providing W, they could cast Seam Rip to exile the Tiger-Seal (mana value 1, which is ≤2). With Multiversal Passage, they'd need to choose a basic land type and either pay 2 life or have it enter tapped, and they still only get one color from it. Hushwood Verge is strictly better here as the turn 2 land drop since it enters untapped for free and enables both colors needed.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Multiversal Passage as the land for turn 2.
annotations.betterLine: Play Hushwood Verge (enters untapped since you control Breeding Pool, a Forest), then cast Llanowar Elves with the green mana, preserving Multiversal Passage for later and keeping the Seam Rip option open with white mana available.

annotations.description: Casting Fear of Missing Out before playing a land drop. Playing a land first (like Riverpyre Verge or Island) costs nothing and provides more mana flexibility in future turns. Additionally, FoMO requires discarding a card, and having more information about sequencing (land first) is generally correct.

annotations.betterLine: Play a land (Island or Riverpyre Verge) first, then cast Fear of Missing Out with the available mana

annotations.description: Fear of Missing Out's enter-the-battlefield trigger requires discarding a card. Discarding the second copy of Fear of Missing Out throws away a powerful card that could be cast later for additional combat phases and card filtering. Discarding a land like Riverpyre Verge or Island would be better since the player already has lands in hand (Multiversal Passage, Island, Riverpyre Verge) and only needs a few more land drops. Keeping Fear of Missing Out gives future options for another threat with delirium synergy.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Riverpyre Verge or Island instead, preserving the second Fear of Missing Out as a future threat. The player has plenty of land options in hand already (Island, Multiversal Passage, Riverpyre Verge). However, discarding Fear of Missing Out does add an enchantment creature type to the graveyard which helps enable delirium for the Fear of Missing Out already on the battlefield, making this somewhat defensible.

annotations.description: GLM47 Spike has 4 mana available (Mountain, Spirebluff Canal, Riverpyre Verge, and Tiger-Seal token) and chose not to cast any spell. Frostcliff Siege costs 1UR and could be cast this turn, providing either card draw on combat damage (Jeskai) or +1/+0, trample, and haste to creatures (Temur). With Fear of Missing Out on board as an attacker, either mode would provide significant value. Winternight Stories (2U) could also be cast to dig through the deck. Passing with full mana available and no reason to hold up mana (Torch the Tower is the only instant and opponent has no creatures) wastes a full turn of development.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to cast any spell, passing with 4 mana open and no meaningful instant-speed plays needed.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Frostcliff Siege (choosing Jeskai to draw cards on combat damage from Fear of Missing Out, or Temur for the power boost) to develop the board. Alternatively, cast Winternight Stories to draw three cards and improve hand quality.

annotations.description: With only 2 lands in play and 3 land cards in hand (Willowrush Verge, Hushwood Verge, Hushwood Verge), the player should play a land before casting spells. Playing a land first (like Willowrush Verge, which can tap for U or G with a Forest in play via Breeding Pool) would allow casting both Llanowar Elves AND another 1-drop (Gene Pollinator or second Llanowar Elves) this turn, or enable casting the 2-mana Badgermole Cub alongside a 1-drop. Casting Llanowar Elves first before playing a land is a sequencing error - though Llanowar Elves only costs {G} which can be paid with existing lands, the player should play a land first to maximize mana available this turn.

annotations.betterLine: Play Willowrush Verge (or Hushwood Verge) first, then cast Llanowar Elves and potentially another 1-drop like Gene Pollinator, maximizing board development with 3 mana available instead of 2
